verses.text: 1:1The proverbs of Solomon son of David, who reigned in Israel,
1:2for knowing wisdom and discipline and understanding words of good sense,
1:3for receiving turns of speech, understanding true righteousness, and directing judgment rightly,
1:4so that he may give shrewdness to the innocent, perception and thought to a young child.
1:5For a wise person who hears these things will become wiser, and the discerning will acquire guidance,
1:6and understand a comparison and an obscure saying, the utterances of the wise and riddles.

1:7The fear of God is the beginning of wisdom, and good understanding belongs to all who practice it. Reverence toward God is the beginning of perception, but the ungodly will despise wisdom and discipline.
1:8Listen, son, to your father’s discipline, and do not reject your mother’s ordinances,
1:9for you will receive a crown of graces for your head and a golden collar around your neck.
1:10Son, do not let ungodly men lead you astray; do not agree if they invite you, saying,
1:11Come with us; share in bloodshed. Let us hide a righteous man in the earth unjustly;
1:12let us swallow him alive like Hades and remove his memory from the earth.
1:13Let us seize his costly property and fill our houses with spoils.
1:14Cast your lot among us; let us all obtain a common purse, and let there be one moneybag for us.
1:15Do not walk in the way with them; turn your foot away from their paths,
1:16for their feet run toward evil, and they are quick to shed blood.
1:17For nets are not unjustly stretched out for winged creatures.
1:18For those who share in murder store up evils for themselves, and the overthrow of lawless men is evil.
1:19These are the ways of all who carry out lawless deeds, for through ungodliness they take away their own life.
1:20Wisdom is celebrated at the exits, and in the squares she speaks openly.
1:21At the tops of walls she is proclaimed; at rulers’ gates she sits nearby, and at city gates she speaks boldly:
1:22As long as the innocent hold to righteousness, they will not be ashamed. But the senseless, desiring insolence, became ungodly and hated perception,
1:23and became liable to reproofs. Behold, I will send forth to you an utterance of my breath, and I will teach you my word.
1:24Since I kept calling and you did not obey, and kept extending words and you paid no attention,
1:25but you were making my counsels ineffective and disobeyed my reproofs,
1:26therefore I too will laugh at your ruin and exult when destruction comes to you,
1:27and when sudden tumult reaches you and overthrow arrives like a storm, when affliction and siege come upon you, or when destruction comes to you.
1:28For when you call upon me, I will not listen to you; evil people will seek me and will not find me,
1:29for they hated wisdom and did not choose the fear of the Lord,
1:30nor did they want to attend to my counsels, but they were sneering at my reproofs.
1:31Therefore they will eat the fruits of their own way and be filled with their own ungodliness.
1:32For because they wronged the innocent, they will be murdered, and examination will destroy the ungodly.
1:33But whoever listens to me will dwell in hope and rest fearlessly from every evil.
2:1Son, if you receive an utterance of my commandment and hide it within yourself,
2:2your ear will obey wisdom, and you will apply your heart to understanding; you will also apply it to admonishing your son.
2:3for if you call upon wisdom and give your voice to understanding, and seek perception with a loud voice,
2:4and if you seek it like silver and search it out like treasures,
2:5then you will understand the fear of the Lord and find the knowledge of God.
2:6For the Lord gives wisdom, and from His presence come knowledge and understanding.
2:7He stores up salvation for those acting rightly; He will shield their journey,
2:8to guard the ways of righteous ordinances, and He will protect the way of those who revere Him.
2:9Then you will understand righteousness and judgment, and you will make all good courses straight.
2:10For if wisdom enters your mind and perception seems good to your soul,
2:11good counsel will guard you, and holy thought will keep you,
2:12so that it may rescue you from an evil way and from a man who says nothing trustworthy.
2:13O you who abandon straight ways to walk in ways of darkness,
2:14who delight in evils and rejoice in evil distortion,
2:15whose paths are crooked and whose tracks are bent,
2:16to put you far from a straight way and make you alien to a righteous judgment.
2:17Son, do not let evil counsel seize you, counsel that abandons the teaching of youth and has forgotten a divine covenant.
2:18For she has set her house beside death and her courses beside Hades with the earthborn.
2:19All who travel in her will not return, nor will they reach straight paths, for they are not reached by years of life.
2:20For if they had walked good paths, they would have found smooth paths of righteousness.
2:21Good people will inhabit the land, and the innocent will remain in it, for the upright will dwell in the land and the holy will remain in it.
2:22The ways of the ungodly will perish from the land, and the lawless will be driven out of it.
3:1Son, do not forget my ordinances; let your heart keep my words,
3:2for they will add length of life, years of living, and peace to you.
3:3Do not let acts of mercy and faithfulness fail you. Fasten them around your neck, and you will find favor.
3:4And take thought for good things before the Lord and people.
3:5Trust God with your whole heart; do not exalt yourself in your own wisdom.
3:6In all your ways acknowledge her, that she may cut your ways straight; and your foot will surely not stumble.
3:7Do not be prudent in your own estimation; fear God and turn away from every evil.
3:8Then there will be healing for your body and care for your bones.
3:9Honor the Lord from your righteous labors, and offer Him firstfruits from your fruits of righteousness,
3:10so that your storerooms may be filled with an abundance of grain and your vats gush with wine.
3:11Son, do not make light of the Lord’s discipline or lose heart when corrected by Him,
3:12for the Lord disciplines the one He loves and scourges every son He receives.
3:13Blessed is the person who found wisdom, the mortal who saw good sense,
3:14for trading in her is better than treasures of gold and silver.
3:15She is more valuable than costly stones; nothing evil will stand against her. She is readily known to all who approach her, and nothing precious is worthy of her.
3:16For length of life and years of living are in her right hand, and wealth and glory in her left.
3:16aRighteousness proceeds from her mouth, and she carries law and mercy on her tongue.
3:17Her ways are good ways, and all her paths are in peace.
3:18She is a tree of life to all who hold her fast, and secure for those who lean on her as on the Lord.
3:19God founded the earth by wisdom and prepared the heavens by good sense.
3:20By perception the deeps were split open, and clouds flowed with dew.
3:21Son, do not drift away; keep my counsel and thought,
3:22so that your soul may live and grace be around your neck.
3:22aThere will be healing for your flesh and care for your bones,
3:23so that you may walk all your ways confidently in peace, and your foot will certainly not stumble.
3:24For if you sit, you will be fearless, and if you sleep, you will sleep pleasantly.
3:25You will not fear an approaching fright or the oncoming assaults of the ungodly,
3:26for the Lord will be upon all your ways and support your foot so that you are not shaken.
3:27Do not refrain from doing good to someone in need whenever your hand has the means to help.
3:28Do not say, ‘Go away and come back; tomorrow I will give,’ when you are able to do good, for you do not know what the coming day will bring forth.
3:29Do not devise evils against your friend who lives nearby and trusts in you.
3:30Do not seek enmity with anyone in vain, lest he do you some harm.
3:31Do not acquire the reproaches of evil men or imitate their ways,
3:32for every lawless person is unclean before the Lord, and he does not sit in council among the righteous.
3:33God’s curse is in the houses of the ungodly, but the dwellings of the righteous are blessed.
3:34The Lord opposes the proud, but gives grace to the humble.
3:35The wise will inherit glory, but the ungodly raised up dishonor.
4:1Listen, children, to a father’s discipline; pay attention to gain discernment,
4:2for I give you a good gift; do not abandon my law.
4:3For I too became a son obedient to a father and loved in a mother’s presence,
4:4who used to speak to me and teach me: Let our word take hold in your heart;
4:5keep commandments; do not forget or disregard an utterance of my mouth,
4:6and do not abandon her, and she will hold fast to you; love her, and she will keep you.
4:8Fortify her, and she will exalt you; honor her so that she may embrace you,
4:9so that she may give your head a crown of graces and shield you with a crown of delight.
4:10Listen, son, and receive my words, and your years of life will multiply, so that many ways of living may be yours,
4:11for I teach you ways of wisdom and lead you onto straight tracks.
4:12For if you walk, your steps will not be shut in, and if you run, you will not grow weary.
4:13Take hold of my discipline; do not release it, but keep it for yourself for your life.
4:14Do not enter the ways of the ungodly or imitate the ways of the lawless.
4:15Wherever they encamp, do not go there; turn away from them and pass by.
4:16For they will not sleep unless they do harm; their sleep has been taken away, and they do not lie down.
4:17For these people eat food of ungodliness and get drunk on lawless wine.
4:18But the ways of the righteous shine like light; they go forward and illuminate until the day comes right.
4:19But the ways of the ungodly are dark; they do not know how they stumble.
4:20Son, attend to my utterance; apply your ear to my words,
4:21so that your springs do not fail you; keep them in your heart,
4:22for there is life for those who find them and healing for all flesh.
4:23With every guard keep your heart, for from these come life’s outlets.
4:24Remove a crooked mouth from yourself and thrust unjust lips far away from you.
4:25Let your eyes look straight, and let your eyelids incline toward righteous things.
4:26Make straight tracks for your feet and direct your ways rightly.
4:27Do not turn to the right or the left; turn your foot away from an evil way.
4:27aFor God knows the ways on the right, but those on the left are perverted.
4:27bHe Himself will make your tracks straight and advance your journeys in peace.
5:1Son, attend to my wisdom, and incline your ear to my words,
5:2so that you may guard good understanding. I command you to heed the discernment of my lips.
5:3Do not attend to a base woman, for honey drips from a prostitute’s lips; for a time she oils your throat.
5:4Afterward, however, you will find it more bitter than gall and sharper than a two-edged blade.
5:5For folly’s feet lead those who engage with her down with death into Hades; her tracks are not firmly set.
5:6For she does not travel life’s ways; her tracks are slippery and not easy to recognize.
5:7Now therefore, son, listen to me, and do not make my words ineffective.
5:8Put your way far from her; do not approach the doors of her houses,
5:9so that you do not surrender your life to others and your livelihood to the merciless,
5:10so that outsiders are not filled with your strength, and your labors enter outsiders’ houses,
5:11and you will come to regret it at the end, when the flesh of your body is worn away,
5:12and you will say, “How I hated discipline! My heart turned aside from rebukes.
5:13I did not listen to the voice of the one disciplining and teaching me, nor incline my ear.
5:14I was nearly in every kind of evil in the midst of the assembly and congregation.”
5:15Drink waters from your vessels and from your spring wells.
5:16Do not let waters overflow for you from your spring; but let your waters travel into your own squares.
5:17Let them belong to you alone, and let no outsider share with you.
5:18Let your fountain of water be your own, and share joy with the wife of your youth.

5:19Let a deer of affection and a colt of your graces keep company with you. Let your own woman lead you and be with you at every time, for as you move in the company of her affection, you will be one among many.
5:20Do not be much involved with another woman, nor be held in the arms of one who is not your own.
5:21For a man’s ways are before God’s eyes, and He watches all his tracks.
5:22Lawless acts hunt a man, and each is bound tight by the cords of his own sins.
5:23He dies among the undisciplined; from the abundance of his own life he was cast out and perished through folly.
6:1Son, if you act as guarantor for your friend, you will give your hand over to an enemy.
6:2For a man’s own lips are a strong trap, and he is caught by the lips of his own mouth.
6:3Son, do what I command you and save yourself—for through your friend you have come into evil men’s hands. Go without growing slack, and press the friend for whom you acted as guarantor.
6:4Give no sleep to your eyes, nor doze with your eyelids,
6:5so that you may save yourself like a gazelle from snares and like a bird from a trap.
6:6Go to the ant, sluggard; see its ways and emulate them, and become wiser than it.
6:7For although it has no cultivated field, and has no one forcing it, and is under no master,
6:8it prepares its food in summer and makes abundant provision at harvest.
6:8aOr go to the bee and learn how industrious she is, and how nobly she performs her work,
6:8bwhose labors kings and private people use for health; she is desired by everyone and held in esteem.
6:8cAlthough weak in bodily strength, she was advanced because she honored wisdom.
6:9How long will you remain lying down, sluggard? When will you rise from sleep?
6:10You sleep a little, sit a little, doze a little, and clasp your chest with your hands a little;
6:11then poverty arrives beside you like an evil traveler, and want like a good runner.
6:11aBut if you are diligent, your harvest will come like a spring, and want will desert you like a bad runner.
6:12A foolish and lawless man travels ways that are not good;
6:13the same man signals with his eye and gives signs with his foot, and instructs by gestures of his fingers;
6:14with a twisted heart he devises evils at every time. Such a person stirs up disturbances for a city.
6:15Therefore his destruction comes suddenly: a cutting down and an incurable crushing,
6:16because he rejoices in everything the Lord hates, and is crushed because of his soul’s uncleanness:
6:17an insolent person’s eye, an unjust tongue, hands shedding a righteous person’s blood,
6:18and a heart devising evil thoughts, and feet hastening to do harm;
6:19an unjust witness kindles falsehoods and sends disputes among brothers.
6:20Son, guard your father’s laws, and do not reject your mother’s ordinances.
6:21Fasten them always upon your soul, and collar them around your neck.
6:22Whenever you walk, take her along and let her be with you; when you sleep, let her guard you, so that when you rise she may converse with you,
6:23because the commandment of law is a lamp and a light, and correction and discipline are life’s way,
6:24to preserve you from a married woman and from an alien tongue’s slander.
6:25Do not let desire for beauty overcome you; do not be hunted by your own eyes, nor seized by her eyelids.
6:26For a prostitute’s price is as much as one loaf, but a woman hunts men’s precious lives.
6:27Will someone bind fire in his bosom without burning his garments?
6:28Or will someone walk on fiery coals without burning his feet?
6:29So is the one who goes in to a married woman: he will not be acquitted, nor will anyone touching her.
6:30It is no wonder if someone is caught stealing, for he steals to fill his appetite when hungry.
6:31But if caught, he will repay sevenfold, and by giving all his possessions he will rescue himself.
6:32But the adulterer, through lack of sense, brings destruction upon his own life;
6:33he bears pains and dishonors, and his reproach will never be wiped away.
6:34For her husband’s anger is full of jealousy; he will not spare on the day of judgment,
6:35he will not trade his enmity for any ransom, nor be reconciled by many gifts.
7:1Son, guard my words, and hide my commandments with yourself.
7:1aSon, honor the Lord and you will be strong; apart from Him, fear no other.
7:2Guard my commandments and you will live, and my words like the pupils of eyes.
7:3Put them around your fingers; inscribe them on the broad surface of your heart.
7:4Say that wisdom is your sister, and acquire understanding as your familiar companion,
7:5so that she may keep you from an alien and wicked woman, if she catches you with pleasing words.
7:6For she leans out from a window of her house toward the squares,
7:7and whenever she sees among the foolish children a young man lacking sense,
7:8passing by a corner in the passages of her houses
7:9and talking in evening darkness, when night is still and murky,
7:10the woman meets him, with a prostitute’s appearance, making young men’s hearts fly away.
7:11She is fluttering with excitement and dissolute; her feet do not rest in the house.
7:12For at one time she roams outside, and at another she lies in wait in the squares, at every corner.
7:13Then she took hold of him and kissed him; with a shameless face she addressed him:
7:14“I have a peace sacrifice; today I am paying my vows.
7:15For this reason I came out to meet you; longing for your face, I have found you.
7:16I have stretched my bed with bands and spread it with double-sided rugs from Egypt.
7:17I have sprinkled my bed with saffron and my house with cinnamon.
7:18Come, let us enjoy affection until dawn; come here, let us roll in love.
7:19For my husband is not at home; he has gone on a long journey,
7:20taking a pouch of silver in his hand; after many days he will return to his house.”
7:21She led him astray with much conversation and drove him off course with snares from her lips.
7:22He followed her, made a fool, as an ox is led to slaughter and as a dog to bonds,
7:23or as a deer struck in the liver by an arrow. He hurries like a bird into a trap, not knowing that he runs for his life.
7:24Now therefore, son, listen to me, and attend to my mouth’s sayings.
7:25Do not let your heart turn aside to her ways.
7:26For she has wounded and brought down many, and those she has murdered are beyond counting.
7:27Her house is ways to Hades, leading down to death’s chambers.
8:1You will proclaim wisdom, so that understanding may heed you.
8:2For she is on the high summits, and stands between the paths.
8:3For she sits beside the gates of rulers, and is praised at the entrances:
8:4“You, O human beings, I summon, and I send forth my voice to the children of humankind.
8:5Understand resourcefulness, you innocent ones; and you uneducated, put your heart into it.
8:6Listen to me, for I will speak noble things, and bring forth upright things from my lips.
8:7For my throat will meditate on truth, and lying lips are detestable before me.
8:8All the words of my mouth are with righteousness; there is nothing crooked or entangled in them.
8:9They are all plain to those who understand, and upright to those who find knowledge.
8:10Take discipline rather than silver, and knowledge above tested gold; choose discernment rather than pure gold.
8:11For wisdom is better than costly stones, and nothing precious is worthy of her.
8:12I, Wisdom, have made counsel my dwelling, and I have called upon knowledge and reflection.
8:13The fear of the Lord hates injustice, insolence and arrogance and the ways of wicked people; and I hate the perverted ways of evil people.
8:14Counsel and security are mine; understanding is mine, and strength is mine.
8:15Through me kings reign, and rulers write righteousness.
8:16Through me great men become great, and through me sovereigns rule the earth.
8:17I love those who love me, and those who seek me will find me.
8:18Wealth and glory belong to me, and possession of many things and righteousness.
8:19It is better to reap me than gold and precious stone, and my produce is better than choice silver.
8:20I walk in ways of righteousness, and move in the midst of paths of just judgment,
8:21so that I may apportion substance to those who love me, and fill their storehouses with good things.
8:21aIf I announce to you the things that happen day by day, I will remember to recount the things from eternity.
8:22The Lord created me as the beginning of His ways, for His works.
8:23Before the age He founded me, in the beginning,
8:24before making the earth and before making the deeps, before the springs of the waters came forth,
8:25before the mountains were established, and before all hills He gives me birth.
8:26The Lord made countries and uninhabited places, and the inhabited extremities of the world beneath heaven.
8:27When He was preparing heaven, I was present with Him, and when He was marking out His own throne upon winds.
8:28When He was making the clouds above strong, and when He was setting the springs of the world beneath heaven secure,
8:29and was making the foundations of the earth strong,
8:30I was beside Him, fitting things together; I was the one in whom He delighted. Day by day I rejoiced before Him at every time,
8:31when He rejoiced after completing the inhabited world, and delighted in the children of humankind.
8:32Now, therefore, son, listen to me.
8:34Happy is the man who will listen to me, and the person who will keep my ways, staying awake at my doors day by day, guarding the posts of my entrances.
8:35For my ways out are ways out to life, and favor is prepared by the Lord.
8:36But those who sin against me act impiously against their own lives, and those who hate me love death.”
9:1Wisdom built herself a house, and set seven pillars beneath it.
9:2She slaughtered her own sacrificial animals, mixed her own wine in a mixing-bowl, and prepared her own table.
9:3She sent her own servants, summoning with a lofty proclamation to the mixing-bowl, saying:
9:4“Whoever is foolish, let him turn aside to me!” And to those lacking understanding she said:
9:5“Come, eat of my loaves, and drink wine that I mixed for you.
9:6Leave foolishness, and you will live; seek understanding, so that you may live, and set insight right in knowledge.”
9:7One who disciplines evil people will receive dishonor for himself, and one who reproves an impious person will bring blame on himself.
9:8Do not reprove evil people, so that they may not hate you; reprove a wise person, and he will love you.
9:9Give a wise person a starting point, and he will be wiser; inform a righteous person, and he will receive still more.
9:10The beginning of wisdom is the fear of the Lord, and the counsel of holy ones is understanding.
9:10aFor knowing the law belongs to a good mind.
9:11For in this way you will live a long time, and years of your life will be added to you.
9:12Son, if you become wise for yourself, you will also be wise for your neighbors; but if you turn out evil, you alone will bear evils.
9:12aOne who leans on lies—he will shepherd winds, and that same person will pursue flying birds.
9:12bFor he has left the ways of his own vineyard, and strayed from the paths of his own cultivated field.
9:12cHe travels through a waterless wilderness and land allotted among thirsty places, and gathers fruitlessness with his hands.
9:13A foolish and brazen woman comes to lack a morsel, she who does not know shame.
9:14She sat at the doors of her own house, on a stool openly in the squares,
9:15calling to those passing by and going straight along their ways:
9:16“Whoever among you is most foolish, let him turn aside to me!” And I urge those lacking understanding, saying:
9:17“Taste hidden loaves with pleasure, and sweet stolen water.”
9:18But he does not know that earth-born ones perish beside her, and he comes upon the ledge of Hades.
9:18aBut leap away; do not linger in the place, and do not fix your eye upon her.
9:18bFor in this way you will cross foreign water and pass over a foreign river.
9:18cBut keep away from foreign water, and do not drink from a foreign spring,
9:18dso that you may live a long time, and years of life may be added to you.
10:1A wise son makes a father glad, but a foolish son is grief to his mother.
10:2Treasures will not profit lawless people, but righteousness will rescue from death.
10:3The Lord will not starve a righteous life, but He will overturn the life of the impious.
10:4Poverty humbles a man, but the hands of the courageous make rich.
10:4aA disciplined son will be wise, and he will use the foolish one as a servant.
10:5An intelligent son was preserved from scorching heat, but a lawless son is ruined by wind at harvest.
10:6The Lord’s blessing is upon the head of the righteous, but untimely mourning will cover the mouth of the impious.
10:7The memory of righteous people is with praises, but the name of the impious is extinguished.
10:8One wise in heart will receive commands, but the unrestrained person who twists things with his lips will be tripped up.
10:9One who walks sincerely walks confidently, but one who perverts his ways will be known.
10:10One who signals with his eyes deceitfully gathers griefs for people, but one who reproves with frankness makes peace.
10:11A fountain of life is in the hand of the righteous, but destruction will cover the mouth of the impious.
10:12Hatred raises strife, but friendship covers all who do not love strife.
10:13One who brings forth wisdom from his lips strikes a man lacking heart with a rod.
10:14Wise people will hide discernment, but the mouth of a rash person draws near to ruin.
10:15The possession of the rich is a fortified city, but the ruin of the impious is poverty.
10:16The works of the righteous produce life, but the fruits of the impious produce sins.
10:17Discipline guards righteous paths of life, but discipline that goes unreproved wanders.
10:18Righteous lips conceal enmity, but those who bring forth abuse are most foolish.
10:19Through much talking you will not escape sin, but by sparing your lips you will be intelligent.
10:20The tongue of the righteous is fire-tested silver, but the heart of the impious will fail.
10:21The lips of the righteous know lofty things, but fools die in want.
10:22The Lord’s blessing is upon the head of the righteous; it makes rich, and sorrow in the heart will certainly not be added to it.
10:23A fool does evil things in laughter, but wisdom gives birth to understanding for a man.
10:24An impious person is swept about in destruction, but the desire of the righteous is acceptable.
10:25When a storm passes by, the impious disappears, but the righteous turns aside and is saved for ever.
10:26As an unripe grape is harmful to teeth and smoke to eyes, so is lawlessness to those who practice it.
10:27The fear of the Lord adds days, but the years of the impious will become few.
10:28Gladness stays long with the righteous, but the hope of the impious perishes.
10:29The fear of the Lord is a stronghold for the devout, but ruin for those who do evil.
10:30The righteous will never give way, but the impious will not inhabit the earth.
10:31The mouth of the righteous drips wisdom, but the tongue of the unjust will be destroyed.
10:32The lips of righteous men drip gracious things, but the mouth of the impious turns away.
11:1Deceitful scales are an abomination before the Lord, but a just weight is acceptable to Him.
11:2Wherever insolence enters, dishonor is there too, but the mouth of the humble meditates on wisdom.
11:3A righteous person, when he died, left regret, but the destruction of the impious is ready at hand and welcomed with joy.
11:5Righteousness cuts blameless paths straight, but impiety falls into injustice.
11:6The righteousness of upright men rescues them, but lawless people are caught in their own destruction.
11:7When a righteous man dies, hope does not perish, but the boast of the impious perishes.
11:8The righteous escapes from the hunt, but the impious is handed over in his place.
11:9In the mouth of the impious is a trap for citizens, but the discernment of the righteous has a good course.
11:10Through the good things of the righteous a city prospered,
11:11but by the mouths of the impious it was razed.
11:12One lacking understanding sneers at citizens, but an intelligent man keeps quiet.
11:13A double-tongued man reveals plans in a council, but one faithful in breath conceals matters.
11:14Those who have no steering fall like leaves, but deliverance is in much counsel.
11:15An evil person does harm when he mixes with a righteous person, and he hates the sound of security.
11:16A gracious woman raises glory for her husband, but a woman who hates righteous things is a throne of dishonor. The lazy become lacking in wealth, but the courageous lean upon wealth.
11:17A merciful man does good to his own life, but the merciless destroys his own body.
11:18The impious does unjust works, but the seed of righteous people is a reward of truth.
11:19A righteous son is born for life, but pursuit of the impious is for death.
11:20Perverted ways are an abomination to the Lord, but all who are blameless in their ways are acceptable to Him.
11:21One who unjustly puts hands into a hand will not go unpunished, but one who sows righteousness will receive a faithful reward.
11:22As a ring in a pig’s snout, so is beauty for a woman of bad judgment.
11:23Every desire of the righteous is good, but the hope of the impious will perish.
11:24There are those who sow their own things and produce more, and there are those who gather and become diminished.
11:25Every blessed life is sincere, but a quick-tempered man is not dignified.
11:26May one who holds grain back leave it to the nations, but blessing is upon the head of one who shares it.
11:27One who devises good things seeks good favor, but evil will overtake the one who searches for it.
11:28One who trusts in wealth will fall, but one who supports righteous people will spring up.
11:29One who does not deal well with his own household will inherit wind, and a fool will serve an intelligent person.
11:30From the fruit of righteousness a tree of life grows, but the lives of lawless people are taken away before their time.
11:31If the righteous is scarcely saved, where will the impious and sinner appear?
12:1One who loves discipline loves discernment, but one who hates rebukes is foolish.
12:2Better is the one who has found favor with the Lord, but a lawless man will be passed over in silence.
12:3A person will not prosper through a lawless person, but the roots of the righteous will not be uprooted.
12:4A courageous woman is a crown to her husband; but as a worm in wood, so a woman who does evil destroys a man.
12:5The reasonings of the righteous are judgments, but the impious steer deceits.
12:6The words of the impious are deceitful, but the mouth of the upright will rescue them.
12:7Wherever he turns, the impious disappears, but the houses of the righteous remain.
12:8The mouth of an understanding person is praised by a man, but one sluggish of heart is sneered at.
12:9Better is a man in dishonor who serves himself than one who clothes himself in honor but needs bread.
12:10The righteous has compassion on the lives of his animals, but the inward affections of the impious are merciless.
12:11One who works his own land will be filled with loaves, but those who pursue empty things lack understanding.
12:11aOne who delights in time spent over wine will leave dishonor in his own strongholds.
12:12The desires of the impious are evil, but the roots of the devout are in strongholds.
12:13Through the sin of lips a sinner falls into traps, but the righteous escapes from them.
12:13aOne who looks gently will receive mercy, but one who confronts people at the gates will crush lives.
12:14From fruits of a mouth a man’s life will be filled with good things, and the recompense of his lips will be given to him.
12:15The ways of fools are upright before them, but a wise person listens to counsel.
12:16A fool announces his anger that same day, but a resourceful person hides his own dishonor.
12:17A righteous person reports demonstrated faithfulness, but the witness of unjust people is deceitful.
12:18There are those who wound with a sword as they speak, but the tongues of the wise heal.
12:19Truthful lips set testimony right, but a hasty witness has an unjust tongue.
12:20Deceit is in the heart of one devising evil things, but those who desire peace will rejoice.
12:21Nothing unjust will please the righteous, but the impious will be filled with evils.
12:22Lying lips are an abomination to the Lord, but one who performs faithful deeds is acceptable to Him.
12:23An understanding man is a throne of discernment, but the heart of fools will meet curses.
12:24The hand of chosen people will rule easily, but deceitful people will become plunder.
12:25A frightening word troubles the heart of a righteous man, but good news makes him glad.
12:26A discerning righteous person will be his own friend, but the judgments of the impious are unreasonable. Evils will pursue those who sin, and the way of the impious will lead them astray.
12:27A deceitful person will not obtain game, but a pure man is a precious possession.
12:28In ways of righteousness is life, but the ways of those who remember wrongs lead to death.
13:1A resourceful son is obedient to a father, but a disobedient son is in destruction.
13:2A good person will eat from fruits of righteousness, but the lives of lawless people will perish before their time.
13:3One who guards his own mouth keeps his own life, but one rash with his lips will terrify himself.
13:4Every idle person is amid desires, but the hands of the courageous are engaged in care.
13:5The righteous hates an unjust word, but the impious is ashamed and will have no frankness.
13:6Righteousness guards the innocent, but sin makes the impious worthless.
13:7There are those who make themselves rich while having nothing, and those who humble themselves amid much wealth.
13:8A man’s own wealth is the ransom of his life, but a poor person does not face a threat.
13:9Light is for the righteous continually, but the light of the impious is extinguished.
13:9aDeceitful lives wander in sins, but the righteous have compassion and show mercy.
13:10An evil person does evil things with insolence, but those who understand themselves are wise.
13:11Property pursued eagerly with lawlessness becomes less, but one who gathers for himself with piety will increase; a righteous person has compassion and lends.
13:12Better is one who begins to help the heart than one who promises and leads it into hope; for a good desire is a tree of life.
13:13One who despises a matter will be despised by it, but one who fears a command is sound.
13:13aNothing good will belong to a deceitful son, but a wise household servant’s actions will prosper, and his way will be made straight.
13:14The law of a wise person is a fountain of life, but the senseless will die by a trap.
13:15Good understanding gives favor, and knowing the law belongs to a good mind, but the ways of the contemptuous are in destruction.
13:16Every resourceful person acts with knowledge, but the fool has spread out his own wickedness.
13:17A rash king will fall into evils, but a faithful messenger will rescue him.
13:18Discipline takes away poverty and dishonor, and one who keeps rebukes will be glorified.
13:19The desires of the devout sweeten the life, but the works of the impious are far from knowledge.
13:20One who walks with the wise will be wise, but one who walks with fools will be known.
13:21Evils will pursue those who sin, but good things will overtake the righteous.
13:22A good man will inherit children’s children, but the wealth of the impious is stored up for the righteous.
13:23The righteous will spend many years in wealth, but the unjust will perish swiftly.
13:24One who spares the staff hates his son, but one who loves him disciplines carefully.
13:25The righteous, by eating, fills his life, but the lives of the impious are in want.
14:1Wise women built houses, but the foolish woman tore them down with her hands.
14:2One who walks uprightly fears the Lord, but one who is crooked in his ways will be dishonored.
14:3From the mouth of fools comes a staff of insolence, but the lips of the wise guard them.
14:4Where there are no oxen, mangers are clean; but where there is much produce, an ox’s strength is evident.
14:5A faithful witness does not lie, but an unjust witness kindles lies.
14:6You will seek wisdom among evil people and not find it, but discernment is readily found among intelligent people.
14:7Everything is against a foolish man, but wise lips are weapons of discernment.
14:8The wisdom of resourceful people will recognize their ways, but the senselessness of fools is in wandering.
14:9The houses of lawless people will owe purification, but the houses of the righteous are acceptable.
14:10A man’s heart is perceptive; his life is sorrowful, but when he rejoices, he does not mingle with insolence.
14:11The houses of the impious will disappear, but the tents of those who act rightly will stand.
14:12There is a way that seems upright to people, but its final outcome comes to the bottom of Hades.
14:13In gladness sorrow does not mingle, but in the end joy comes to mourning.
14:14One rash in heart will be filled from his own ways, but a good man from his own thoughts.
14:15The innocent person believes every word, but the resourceful comes to reconsideration.
14:16The wise, becoming afraid, turned from evil, but the fool, trusting himself, mixes with a lawless person.
14:17One quick to anger acts without counsel, but an intelligent man endures many things.
14:18Fools will receive a share of wickedness, but the resourceful will lay hold of discernment.
14:19Evil people will slip before good people, and the impious will attend the doors of the righteous.
14:20Friends will hate poor friends, but the friends of the rich are many.
14:21One who dishonors the needy sins, but one who has mercy on the poor is blessed.
14:22Those who wander devise evil things, but good people devise mercy and truth. Makers of evils do not know mercy and faithfulness, but acts of mercy and faithfulness are with good makers.
14:23In everyone who takes care there is abundance, but the pleasure-loving and unfeeling person will be in want.
14:24A resourceful person is the crown of the wise, but the occupation of fools is evil.
14:25A faithful witness will rescue a life from evils, but a deceitful person kindles lies.
14:26In the fear of the Lord is hope of strength, and he leaves a support for his children.
14:27The command of the Lord is a fountain of life, and it causes one to turn from a trap of death.
14:28In a numerous nation is a king’s glory, but in the failing of a people is a ruler’s ruin.
14:29A patient man is great in understanding, but one faint of spirit is exceedingly foolish.
14:30A gentle-tempered man is a physician of the heart, but a perceptive heart is a moth to the bones.
14:31One who extorts from the needy provokes the One who made him, but one who honors Him has mercy on the poor.
14:32The impious will be thrust away in his wickedness, but one trusting in his own piety is righteous.
14:33Wisdom is in a man’s good heart, but in the heart of fools it is not discerned.
14:34Righteousness exalts a nation, but sins diminish tribes.
14:35An intelligent attendant is acceptable to a king, and by his own skill he removes dishonor.
15:1Anger destroys even intelligent people; but a yielding answer turns away wrath, and a painful word stirs up anger.
15:2The tongue of the wise knows good things, but the mouth of fools will announce evil things.
15:3The eyes of the Lord are in every place; they observe both evil people and good people.
15:4Healing of a tongue is a tree of life, but one who keeps watch over it will be filled with spirit.
15:5A fool sneers at a father’s discipline, but one who keeps commands is more resourceful.

15:6In abundant righteousness is great strength, but the impious will perish from the earth, roots and all. In the houses of the righteous is great strength, but the fruits of the impious will perish.
15:7The lips of the wise are bound to discernment, but the hearts of fools are not secure.
15:8The sacrifices of the impious are an abomination to the Lord, but the prayers of those going straight are acceptable to Him.
15:9The ways of the impious are an abomination to the Lord, but He loves those who pursue righteousness.
15:10The discipline of an innocent person is recognized by passersby, but those who hate rebukes die shamefully.
15:11Hades and destruction are manifest before the Lord; how are human hearts not also?
15:12An uneducated person will not love those who reprove him, and he will not associate with the wise.
15:13When the heart rejoices, the face flourishes, but when it is in sorrows, the face grows gloomy.
15:14An upright heart seeks discernment, but the mouth of the uneducated will know evil things.
15:15All the time the eyes of evil people expect evils, but good people rest quietly continually.
15:16Better a small portion with the fear of the Lord than great storehouses with fearlessness.
15:17Better hospitality of vegetables with friendship and favor than a serving of calves with enmity.
15:18A quick-tempered man prepares battles, but a patient person calms even a battle about to begin.
15:18aA patient man will extinguish disputes, but the impious stirs them up still more.
15:19The ways of the idle are strewn with thorns, but those of the courageous are well worn.
15:20A wise son makes a father glad, but a foolish son sneers at his mother.
15:21The paths of a senseless person lack understanding, but an intelligent man walks making his course straight.
15:22Those who do not honor councils put plans off, but counsel remains in the hearts of those who deliberate.
15:23The evil person will certainly not heed it, nor say anything timely and good for the community.
15:24The thoughts of an understanding person are ways of life, so that, turning aside from Hades, he may be saved.
15:25The Lord pulls down the houses of the insolent, but He established the boundary of a widow.
15:26An unjust thought is an abomination to the Lord, but the sayings of pure people are noble.
15:27One who takes bribes destroys himself, but one who hates taking gifts is saved.
15:27aBy acts of mercy and faithfulness sins are thoroughly cleansed, and by the fear of the Lord everyone turns from evil.
15:28The hearts of the righteous meditate on faithful things, but the mouth of the impious answers evil things.
15:28aThe ways of righteous men are acceptable to the Lord, and through them even enemies become friends.
15:29God is far distant from the impious, but He listens to the prayers of the righteous.
15:29aBetter a small gain with righteousness than much produce with injustice.
15:29bLet a man’s heart consider righteous things, so that his steps may be set right by God.
15:30An eye looking at good things gladdens the heart, and a good report makes bones full.
15:32One who thrusts discipline away hates himself, but one who keeps rebukes loves his own life.
15:33The fear of God is discipline and wisdom, and the beginning of glory will answer her.
16:2All the works of the humble are manifest before God, but the impious will perish on an evil day.
16:5Everyone high of heart is unclean before God, and one who unjustly puts hands into a hand will not be acquitted.
16:7The beginning of a good way is to do righteous things, and these are more acceptable before God than sacrificing sacrifices.
16:8One who seeks the Lord will find knowledge with righteousness, and those who seek Him rightly will find peace.
16:9All the works of the Lord are with righteousness, but the impious is kept for an evil day.
16:10An oracle is on the lips of a king, and his mouth will certainly not go astray in judgment.
16:11The balance’s inclination is righteousness before the Lord, and His works are just weights.
16:12One who does evil is an abomination to a king, for a throne of rule is prepared with righteousness.
16:13Righteous lips are acceptable to a king, and he loves upright words.
16:14A king’s wrath is a messenger of death, but a wise man will appease him.
16:15In the light of life is a king’s son, and those acceptable to him are like a cloud of late rain.
16:16Nests of wisdom are more desirable than gold, and nests of understanding more desirable than silver.

16:17Paths of life turn aside from evils, and ways of righteousness are length of life. One who receives discipline will be amid good things, and one who keeps rebukes will be made wise. One who guards his own ways keeps his own life, and one who loves his life will spare his mouth.
16:18Insolence leads before ruin, and evil-mindedness before a fall.
16:19Better a gentle-tempered person with humility than one who divides spoils with the insolent.
16:20One understanding in matters is a finder of good things, and one trusting in God is blessed.
16:21They call the wise and understanding worthless, but those sweet in speech will hear more.
16:22Reflection is a fountain of life to those who possess it, but the discipline of fools is evil.
16:23A wise person’s heart will understand what comes from his own mouth, and will carry discernment upon his lips.
16:24Good words are honeycombs, and their sweetness is healing of the life.
16:25There are ways that seem upright to a man, but their final outcome looks toward the bottom of Hades.
16:26A man in toils toils for himself and forces his own destruction upon himself; but the crooked person carries destruction upon his own mouth.
16:27A foolish man digs evils for himself, and upon his own lips stores up fire.
16:28A crooked man sends out evils, lights a torch of deceit for evil people, and separates friends.
16:29A lawless man puts friends to the test, and leads them away into ways that are not good.
16:30Fixing his eyes, he considers perverted things, and with his lips determines all evils; this man is a furnace of wickedness.
16:31Old age is a crown of boasting, and it is found in ways of righteousness.
16:32A patient man is better than a strong man, and one who controls anger is better than one who captures a city.
16:33Everything comes into the laps of the unjust, but all righteous things are from the Lord.
17:1Better a morsel with pleasure in peace than a house full of many good things and unjust sacrifices with battle.
17:2An intelligent household servant will rule foolish masters, and divide portions among brothers.
17:3As silver and gold are tested in a furnace, so hearts are chosen before the Lord.
17:4An evil person heeds the tongue of lawless people, but a righteous person pays no attention to lying lips.
17:5One who laughs at the poor provokes the One who made him, and one who rejoices over someone perishing will not be acquitted; but one who has compassion will receive mercy.
17:6The crown of elders is children’s children, and the boast of children is their fathers.
17:6aThe whole world of possessions belongs to the faithful person, but not even an obol belongs to the unfaithful.
17:7Faithful lips will not suit a fool, nor lying lips a righteous person.
17:8Discipline is a reward of favors to those who use it, and wherever it turns, it will prosper.
17:9One who hides wrongdoings seeks friendship, but one who hates hiding them separates friends and household members.
17:10A threat crushes an intelligent person’s heart, but a fool, though whipped, does not perceive.
17:11Every evil person raises disputes, but the Lord will send a merciless messenger to him.
17:12Concern will fall upon an intelligent man, but fools will deliberate evil things.
17:13One who repays evil things instead of good things—evils will not move from his house.
17:14The beginning of righteousness gives authority to words, but faction and battle lead the way to want.
17:15One who judges the unjust righteous and the righteous unjust is unclean and detestable before God.
17:16Why did possessions come to a fool? For one lacking heart will not be able to acquire wisdom.
17:16aOne who makes his own house high seeks ruin, and one who turns crookedly away from learning will fall into evils.
17:17Let a friend be yours at all times, and let brothers be useful in times of need; for this is why they are born.
17:18A foolish man claps and rejoices over himself, as does one who acts as guarantor for his own friend with a pledge.
17:19One who loves sin rejoices in battles,
17:20but one hard of heart does not meet good things. A man changeable in tongue will fall into evils,
17:21and a fool’s heart is pain to the one who possesses it. A father does not rejoice over an uneducated son, but an intelligent son gladdens his mother.
17:22A rejoicing heart makes one flourish, but a sorrowful man’s bones dry up.
17:23The ways of one taking gifts unjustly in his lap do not prosper, and an impious person bends the ways of righteousness.
17:24An understanding face belongs to a wise man, but the fool’s eyes are upon the extremities of the earth.
17:25A foolish son is anger to a father, and pain to the one who bore him.
17:26To penalize a righteous man is not good, nor is it holy to plot against righteous rulers.
17:27One who refrains from sending forth a harsh word is discerning, and a patient man is intelligent.
17:28Wisdom will be reckoned to a senseless person who asks for wisdom, and someone who makes himself mute will seem intelligent.
18:1A man who wishes to separate from friends seeks pretexts, and at every time he will be subject to reproach.
18:2One lacking understanding has no use for wisdom, for he is led rather by foolishness.
18:3When the impious comes into the depth of evils, he despises, and dishonor and reproach come upon him.
18:4A word in a man’s heart is deep water, and a river springs up, a fountain of life.
18:5To admire the face of the impious is not good, nor is it holy to turn aside what is just in judgment.
18:6A fool’s lips lead him into evils, and his rash mouth calls upon death.
18:7A fool’s mouth is ruin for him, and his lips are a trap for his life.
18:8Fear casts down the lazy, and the lives of womanish men will hunger.
18:9One who does not heal himself in his works is brother to one who ruins himself.
18:10From greatness of strength comes the name of the Lord, and righteous people who run to it are raised high.
18:11A rich man’s property is a fortified city, and its glory casts a great shadow.
18:12Before ruin a man’s heart is raised high, and before glory it is humbled.
18:13One who answers a word before hearing it—it is foolishness and reproach for him.
18:14An intelligent attendant calms a man’s anger, but who will bear a fainthearted man?
18:15An intelligent heart acquires discernment, and the ears of the wise seek reflection.
18:16A person’s gift makes space for him, and seats him beside rulers.
18:17The righteous is his own accuser in the opening speech, but when the opponent presses in, he is reproved.
18:18A lot stops disputes, and makes a determination among rulers.
18:19A brother helped by a brother is like a fortified and high city, and is strong like a founded palace.
18:20From fruits of a mouth a man fills his belly, and from fruits of his lips he will be filled.
18:21Death and life are in the hand of the tongue, and those who control it will eat its fruits.
18:22One who found a good wife found favors, and received gladness from God.
18:22aOne who casts out a good wife casts out good things, but one who keeps an adulteress is foolish and impious.
19:3A man’s foolishness ruins his ways, but in his heart he blames God.
19:4Wealth adds many friends, but the poor person is abandoned even by the friend he has.
19:5A false witness will not be unpunished, and one who accuses unjustly will not escape.
19:6Many attend the faces of kings, but every evil person becomes a reproach to a man.

19:7Everyone who hates a poor brother will also be far from friendship. A good thought will draw near to those who know it, and an intelligent man will find it. One who does many evils brings wickedness to completion, and one who provokes words will not be saved.
19:8One who acquires understanding loves himself, and one who keeps understanding will find good things.
19:9A false witness will not be unpunished, and whoever kindles wickedness will perish by it.
19:10Luxury does not benefit a fool, nor does it benefit a household servant if he begins to rule with insolence.
19:11A merciful man is patient, and his boast comes upon lawless people.
19:12A king’s threat is like a lion’s growling, but as dew upon grass, so is his cheerfulness.
19:13A foolish son is shame to a father, and prayers from a courtesan’s fee are not pure.
19:14Fathers apportion house and property to children, but a wife is joined to a husband by God.
19:15Cowardice holds a womanish man, and the life of an idle person will hunger.
19:16One who keeps a command guards his own life, but one who despises his own ways will perish.
19:17One who has mercy on the poor lends to God, and He will repay him according to his gift.
19:18Discipline your son, for in this way he will be hopeful, but do not lift yourself in your soul toward insolence.
19:19An evil-minded man will suffer many penalties, and if he acts pestilentially, he will add his own life as well.
19:20Listen, son, to your father’s discipline, so that you may become wise in your latter days.
19:21Many are the reasonings in a man’s heart, but the counsel of the Lord remains for ever.
19:22Mercy is a man’s fruit, and better a righteous poor person than a rich liar.
19:23The fear of the Lord is for a man’s life, but the fearless person will lodge in places where knowledge is not attended to.
19:24One who unjustly hides his hands in his lap will certainly not even bring them to his mouth.
19:25When a pestilent person is whipped, a fool becomes more resourceful; but if you reprove an intelligent man, he will understand discernment.
19:26One who dishonors a father and thrusts his mother away will be put to shame and be subject to reproach.
19:27A son who falls short of keeping a father’s discipline will meditate on evil sayings.
19:28One who acts as guarantor for a foolish child treats just judgment with insolence, and the mouth of the impious swallows judgments.
19:29Whips are prepared for the undisciplined, and punishments for the shoulders of fools.
20:1Wine is undisciplined, and drunkenness insolent, and everyone who mingles with it will not be wise.
20:2A king’s threat does not differ at all from a lion’s wrath, and one who provokes him sins against his own life.
20:3It is glory for a man to turn away from abuse, but every fool entangles himself in such things.
20:4A lazy person, when reproached, is not ashamed, and neither is one who borrows grain at harvest.
20:5Counsel in a man’s heart is deep water, but an intelligent man will draw it out.
20:6A human being is a great thing, and a merciful man a precious thing, but finding a faithful man is hard work.
20:7One who lives blamelessly in righteousness will leave his children blessed.
20:8When a righteous king sits on a throne, no evil thing sets itself against him before his eyes.
20:9Who will boast that he has a pure heart? Or who will speak confidently of being clean from sins?
20:9aThe lamp of one who speaks evil of a father or mother will be extinguished, and the pupils of his eyes will see darkness.
20:9bA portion eagerly pursued at first will not be blessed at the end.
20:9cDo not say, “I will punish the enemy.” But wait for the Lord, so that He may help you.
20:10A large weight and a small one, and double measures—both are unclean before the Lord.
20:11And one who makes them will be fettered in his practices; a young man is with a devout person, and his way is straight.
20:12An ear hears and an eye sees; both are works of the Lord.
20:13Do not love speaking against others, so that you are not cut off; open your eyes and be filled with loaves.
20:23A double weight is an abomination to the Lord, and deceitful scales are not good before Him.
20:24A man’s steps are directed by the Lord, but how could a mortal understand his ways?
20:25It is a trap for a man quickly to consecrate something of his own, for after making the vow comes reconsideration.
20:26A wise king is a winnower of the impious, and will bring a wheel upon them.
20:27The breath of human beings is the light of the Lord, who searches the store-chambers of the belly.
20:28Mercy and truth are a guard for a king, and they will surround his throne in righteousness.
20:29Wisdom is an adornment for young men, and gray hair is the glory of elders.
20:30Bruises and crushing wounds meet evil people, and blows reach the store-chambers of the belly.
21:1As a rush of water, so is a king’s heart in God’s hand; wherever He willingly inclines, there He has bent it.
21:2Every man appears righteous to himself, but the Lord sets hearts straight.
21:3Doing righteous things and speaking truth are more pleasing before God than the blood of sacrifices.
21:4One lofty-minded in insolence is rash-hearted, and the lamp of the impious is sin.
21:6One who works up stores with a false tongue pursues empty things toward traps of death.
21:7Destruction will lodge with the impious, for they do not wish to do righteous things.
21:8God sends crooked ways to the crooked, for His works are pure and upright.
21:9Better to dwell on a corner in the open air than in plastered rooms with injustice and in a shared house.
21:10The life of the impious will receive mercy from none of humankind.
21:11When an undisciplined person is penalized, the innocent becomes more resourceful, and a wise person who understands will receive knowledge.
21:12A righteous person understands the hearts of the impious, and brings the impious low amid evils.
21:13One who blocks his ears from hearing the weak will himself also call, and there will be no one listening.
21:14A secret gift overturns anger, but one who is sparing with gifts raises fierce wrath.
21:15Doing judgment is the joy of the righteous, but a devout person is unclean in the eyes of evildoers.
21:16A man who wanders from the way of righteousness will rest in the assembly of giants.
21:17A needy man loves gladness, loving wine and oil toward wealth;
21:18but a lawless person is a cleansing-offering for the righteous.
21:19Better to dwell in a desert land than with a battling, talkative, and quick-tempered woman.
21:20Desirable treasure will rest upon a wise person’s mouth, but foolish men will swallow it down.
21:21A way of righteousness and mercy will find life and glory.
21:22A wise person mounted fortified cities, and brought down the stronghold in which the impious trusted.
21:23One who guards his mouth and tongue keeps his life from affliction.
21:24A rash, self-willed, boastful person is called pestilent, and one who remembers wrongs is lawless.
21:25Desires kill a lazy person, for his hands do not choose to do anything.
21:26The impious desires evil desires the whole day, but the righteous shows mercy and compassion without sparing.
21:27The sacrifices of the impious are an abomination to the Lord, for they offer them lawlessly.
21:28A false witness will perish, but an obedient man will speak with caution.
21:29An impious man stands his ground with a shameless face, but the upright himself understands his ways.
21:30There is no wisdom, there is no courage, there is no counsel with the impious.
21:31A horse is prepared for a day of war, but help is from the Lord.
22:1A good name is more desirable than much wealth, and good favor is above silver and gold.
22:2Rich and poor met one another, and the Lord made both.
22:3A resourceful person, seeing an evil person severely punished, is himself instructed, but fools passed by and were penalized.
22:4The offspring of wisdom is the fear of the Lord, and wealth and glory and life.
22:5Thistles and traps are in crooked ways, but one who guards his own life will keep away from them.
22:7The rich will rule the poor, and household servants will lend to their own masters.
22:8One who sows worthless things will reap evils, and he will bring the blow of his works to completion.
22:8aGod blesses a cheerful and giving man, and He will bring the emptiness of his works to an end.
22:9One who has mercy on the poor will himself be nourished, for he gave of his own loaves to the poor.
22:9aOne who has given gifts obtains victory and honor, yet takes away the life of those who possess them.
22:10Cast a pestilent person out of a council, and strife will go out with him; for whenever he sits in a council, he dishonors everyone.
22:11The Lord loves devout hearts, and all the blameless are acceptable to Him; a king shepherds with his lips.
22:12The eyes of the Lord preserve discernment, but a lawless person makes words worthless.
22:13The lazy person makes an excuse and says, “A lion is in the roads, and murderers in the squares!”
22:14The mouth of a lawless person is a deep pit, and one hated by the Lord will fall into it.
22:14aThere are evil ways before a man, and he does not love turning from them; but one must turn from a crooked and evil way.
22:15Senselessness is fastened to a young person’s heart, but rod and discipline are far from him.
22:16One who extorts from the needy makes his own things many, but gives to the rich at a loss.
22:17Bring your ear beside words of the wise and hear my word, and direct your heart so that you may know that they are good;
22:18and if you put them into your heart, they will gladden you together upon your lips,
22:19so that your hope may be in the Lord, and He may make His way known to you.
22:20And you, copy them for yourself threefold, for counsel and knowledge upon the breadth of your heart.
22:21Therefore I teach you to heed a true word and good knowledge, so as to answer words of truth to those who put questions to you.
22:22Do not use force against the needy, for he is poor, and do not dishonor the weak at the gates;
22:23for the Lord will judge his case, and you will preserve your own life unplundered.
22:24Do not be a companion to a quick-tempered man, and do not lodge with an angry friend,
22:25lest you learn his ways and take nooses for your own life.
22:26Do not give yourself as a pledge out of deference to a face.
22:27For if you have no means from which to pay, they will take the bedding from beneath your sides.
22:28Do not move everlasting boundaries that your fathers set.
22:29A perceptive man, keen in his works, must stand beside kings and not stand beside sluggish men.
23:1If you sit to dine at the table of rulers, thoughtfully consider what is set before you,
23:2and lay your hand to it, knowing that you must prepare such things;
23:3but if you are more insatiable, do not desire his foods, for these belong to a false life.
23:4Do not stretch yourself, being poor, to match a rich man, but hold back in your own reflection;
23:5If you fix your eye upon him, he will appear nowhere, for wings like an eagle’s have been prepared for him, and he returns to the house of the one who presides over him.
23:6Do not dine with a begrudging man, and do not desire his foods,
23:7for as if someone swallowed a hair, so he eats and drinks.
23:8Do not bring him in to yourself and eat your morsel with him, for he will vomit it and ruin your good words.
23:9Say nothing into a fool’s ears, lest he sneer at your intelligent words.
23:10Do not move everlasting boundaries, and do not enter orphans’ property,
23:11for the Lord who redeems them is mighty, and He will judge their case with you.
23:12Give your heart to discipline, and prepare your ears for words of discernment.
23:13Do not refrain from disciplining a little child, for if you strike him with a rod, he will certainly not die;
23:14for you will strike him with a rod, but rescue his life from death.
23:15Son, if your heart becomes wise, you will gladden my heart too,
23:16and your lips will spend time in words with my lips, if the words are upright.
23:17Do not let your heart envy sinners, but be in the fear of the Lord the whole day;
23:18for if you keep these things, you will have offspring, and your hope will not depart.
23:19Listen, son, and become wise, and straighten the reflections of your heart.
23:20Do not be a wine-drinker, and do not stretch yourself over contributions and purchases of meat;
23:21for every drunkard and frequenter of prostitutes will become poor, and every sleepy person will clothe himself in torn and ragged things.
23:22Listen, son, to the father who begot you, and do not despise your mother because she has grown old.
23:24A righteous father brings up well, and his life rejoices over a wise son;
23:25let father and mother rejoice over you, and let the one who bore you be glad.
23:26Give me your heart, son, and let your eyes keep my ways;
23:27for another’s house is a jar with holes, and another’s well is narrow;
23:28for this will swiftly perish, and every lawless person will be consumed.
23:29Who has woe? Who has uproar? Who has a lawsuit? Who has unpleasantness and chatter? Who has bruises for nothing? Whose eyes are livid?
23:30Is it not those who linger over wines? Is it not those who track down where drinking parties take place?
23:31Do not become drunk with wine, but associate with righteous people, and converse during walks; for if you give your eyes to bowls and cups, afterward you will walk about barer than a pestle.
23:32But at the end he lies stretched out as though struck by a snake, and as though by a horned viper its poison spreads through him.
23:33When your eyes see another woman, then your mouth will speak crooked things,
23:34and you will lie down as in the heart of the sea, and like a helmsman in heavy surging;
23:35and you will say, “They strike me, and I felt no pain; they mocked me, but I did not know. When will dawn come, so that I may go and seek those with whom I will gather?”
24:1Son, do not envy evil men, and do not desire to be with them;
24:2for their heart meditates lies, and their lips speak toils.
24:3With wisdom a house is built, and with understanding it is raised upright;
24:4with discernment store-rooms are filled from every precious and good wealth.
24:5A wise person is better than a strong one, and a man with understanding than a great cultivated estate;
24:6with steering war takes place, and help is with a deliberative heart.
24:7Wisdom and good reflection are in the gates of the wise; the wise do not turn from the mouth of the Lord,
24:8but deliberate in councils. Death meets the uneducated,
24:9and a fool dies in sins; and impurity will be defiled in a pestilent man,
24:10on an evil day and on a day of affliction, until he fails.
24:11Rescue those being led to death, and ransom those being killed; do not hold back.

24:12But if you say, “I do not know this person,” know that the Lord knows everyone’s hearts, and the One who fashioned breath for all Himself knows everything, and repays each one according to his works.
24:13Eat honey, son, for a honeycomb is good, so that your throat may be sweetened;
24:14in this way you will perceive wisdom for your own life; for if you find it, your end will be good, and hope will not abandon you.
24:15Do not bring an impious person to the pasture of the righteous, and do not be deceived by a filled belly;
24:16for the righteous will fall seven times and rise, but the impious will grow weak amid evils.
24:17If your enemy falls, do not rejoice over him, and at his tripping do not lift yourself up,
24:18for the Lord will see, and it will not please Him, and He will turn His wrath away from him.
24:19Do not rejoice over evildoers, and do not envy sinners;
24:20for evil people will certainly have no offspring, and the lamp of the impious will be extinguished.
24:21Fear God, son, and the king, and disobey neither of them;
24:22for suddenly they will punish the impious, and who will know the punishments of both?
24:22aA son who guards a word will be outside destruction, and receiving it, he has received it.
24:22bLet no falsehood from a tongue be spoken to a king, and no falsehood will ever come from his tongue.
24:22cA king’s tongue is a sword and is not made of flesh, and whoever is handed over will be crushed;
24:22dfor if his wrath is sharpened, it consumes human beings with their sinews,
24:22eand devours human bones, and burns them together like a flame, so that they are inedible to young eagles.
30:1Fear my words, son, and receive them and repent. Thus says the man to those who trust in God, and I cease:
30:2For I am the most foolish of all people, and human understanding is not in me.
30:3God has taught me wisdom, and knowledge of holy ones I have known.

30:4Who went up to heaven and came down? Who gathered winds in a fold of his garment? Who wrapped water in a cloak? Who took hold of all the ends of the earth? What is his name, or what is his children’s name, so that you may know?
30:5All God’s words have been refined by fire, and He shields those who revere Him.
30:6Do not add to His words, so that He may not reprove you and you become false.
30:7Two things I ask from Thee; do not take favor away from me before I die:
30:8Put a vain and false word far from me; give me neither wealth nor poverty; assign me what is needed and sufficient,
30:9so that I may not become full and false and say, “Who sees me?” or become poor and steal and swear by the name of God.
30:10Do not hand a household servant over into a master’s hands, lest he curse you and you be destroyed.
30:11Evil offspring curse a father and do not bless the mother.
30:12Evil offspring judge themselves righteous, but have not washed away their discharge.
30:13Evil offspring have lofty eyes and exalt themselves with their eyelids.
30:14Evil offspring have swords for teeth and cutting blades for molars, to consume and devour the lowly from the earth and their poor from among people.
24:23These things I say to you, the wise, to recognize: to show deference to a face in judgment is not good;
24:24One who says of the impious, “He is righteous,” will be accursed among peoples and hated among nations;
24:25but those who reprove will appear better, and a good blessing will come upon them;
24:26and lips answering good words will kiss.
24:27Prepare your works for going out, and make yourself ready for the field, and follow behind me, and you will rebuild your house.
24:28Do not be a false witness against your fellow citizen, and do not make your lips wide;
24:29Do not say, “As he treated me, I will treat him, and I will punish him for the wrong he did me.”
24:30A foolish man is like a cultivated field, and a person lacking understanding like a vineyard;
24:31if you leave him alone, he will become wasteland, and grow wild with grass all over and become abandoned, and his stone fences are torn down.
24:32Afterward I reconsidered; I looked so as to choose discipline.
24:33“A little I doze, a little I sleep, a little I clasp my chest with my hands”—
24:34but if you do this, your poverty will come marching in front, and your want like a good runner.

verses.text: 30:15The leech had three daughters, dearly loved, and these three did not fill her, and the fourth was not content to say, “Enough!”
30:16Hades and a woman’s desire, and Tartarus and land not filled with water, and water and fire will certainly not say, “It is enough.”
30:17An eye mocking a father and dishonoring a mother’s old age—may ravens from the ravines peck it out, and may young eagles devour it.
30:18Three things are impossible for me to understand, and the fourth I do not comprehend:
30:19the tracks of a flying eagle, and the ways of a snake upon a rock, and the paths of a seagoing ship, and the ways of a man in youth.
30:20Such is the way of an adulterous woman: when she has acted, she washes herself and says she has done nothing improper.
30:21Through three things the earth is shaken, and it cannot bear the fourth:
30:22if a household servant becomes king, and a fool is filled with food,
30:23and if a maidservant casts out her own mistress, and if a hated woman obtains a good husband.
30:24Four things are smallest upon the earth, yet these are wiser than the wise:
30:25the ants, which have no strength, yet prepare their food in summer;
30:26and the rock badgers, a nation without strength, which made their own houses in rocks;
30:27the locust is without a king, yet marches out in good order at one command;
30:28And the lizard, bracing itself with its hands and being easily caught, lives in a king’s fortifications.
30:29Three things go on their way well, and the fourth moves beautifully:
30:30a lion’s cub, stronger than beasts, which does not turn back or shrink from a beast;
30:31and a spirited rooster walking among hens, and a male goat leading a flock, and a king addressing a nation.
30:32If you give yourself over to merriment and stretch out your hand with fighting, you will be dishonored.
30:33Milk out milk, and there will be butter; but if you squeeze nostrils, blood will come out; and if you drag out words, disputes and battles will come out.

verses.text: 31:1My words have been spoken by God, an oracle concerning a king whom his mother instructed.
31:2What will you keep, child? What? God’s sayings. Firstborn, I speak to you, son. What, child of my womb? What, child of my vows?
31:3Do not give women your wealth, or your mind and livelihood to belated counsel.
31:4Do everything with counsel; drink wine with counsel. The powerful are hot-tempered, but let them not drink wine,
31:5so that, after drinking, they may not forget wisdom and become entirely unable to judge the weak rightly.
31:6Give intoxicating drink to those in grief, and wine to drink to those in pain,
31:7so that they may forget their poverty and no longer remember their troubles.
31:8Open your mouth for God’s word, and judge everyone soundly.
31:9Open your mouth and judge justly, and decide the case of the poor and weak.

verses.text: 25:1These are Solomon’s undifferentiated instructions, which the friends of Hezekiah, king of Judea, copied out.
25:2God’s glory conceals a word, but a king’s glory honors matters.
25:3Heaven is high and earth deep, but a king’s heart is beyond examination.
25:4Beat unapproved silver, and it will be cleansed, entirely pure;
25:5Kill the impious from before a king, and his throne will prosper in righteousness.
25:6Do not boast before a king, and do not station yourself in the places of rulers;
25:7for it is better for you to be told, “Come up to me,” than for him to humble you before a ruler. Say what your eyes have seen.
25:8Do not rush quickly into battle, so that you do not regret it at the end. When your friend reproaches you,
25:9withdraw backward; do not show contempt,
25:10lest the friend reproach you, and your battle and enmity not depart, but be for you equal to death.
25:10aFavor and friendship set one free; keep these for yourself so that you do not become subject to reproach, but guard your ways with readiness to be reconciled.
25:11A golden apple on a carnelian necklace—so is speaking a word.
25:12A costly carnelian is fastened into a golden earring—a wise word into a receptive ear.
25:13As snow coming forth benefits people in harvest heat, so a faithful messenger benefits those who sent him; for he benefits the lives of those who employ him.
25:14Like winds and clouds and very conspicuous rains, so are those who boast of a false gift.
25:15In patience is prosperity for kings, and a soft tongue crushes bones.
25:16Having found honey, eat what is sufficient, lest you become full and vomit.
25:17Bring your foot rarely to your own friend, lest he become filled with you and hate you.
25:18A club and sword and barbed arrow—so also is a man testifying false testimony against his friend.
25:19An evil person’s tooth and a lawless person’s foot will perish on an evil day.
25:20As vinegar is unsuitable for a wound, so a suffering that falls upon the body pains the heart.
25:20aAs a moth harms a garment and a worm wood, so a man’s grief harms the heart.
25:21If your enemy is hungry, feed him; if he is thirsty, give him drink;
25:22for by doing this you will heap coals of fire upon his head, and the Lord will repay you good things.
25:23A north wind raises clouds, but a shameless face provokes a tongue.
25:24Better to dwell on a corner of a roof than with an abusive wife in a shared house.
25:25As cold water is welcome to a thirsty life, so is good news from a faraway land.
25:26As if someone blocked a spring and ruined an outlet of water, so it is disorderly for a righteous person to have fallen before the impious.
25:27Eating much honey is not good, but one must honor glorious words.
25:28As a city with its walls cast down and unwalled, so is a man who does something without counsel.

verses.text: 26:1Like dew at harvest and rain in summer, so honor does not belong to a fool.
26:2As birds and sparrows fly, so an empty curse will come upon no one.
26:3As a whip for a horse and a goad for a donkey, so a rod for a lawless nation.
26:4Do not answer a fool in relation to his foolishness, so that you do not become like him;
26:5but answer a fool according to his foolishness, so that he does not appear wise to himself.
26:6One who sends a word through a foolish messenger will drink reproach from his own feet.
26:7Remove walking from legs, and a proverb from the mouth of fools.
26:8One who binds a stone in a sling is like one who gives glory to a fool.
26:9Thorns grow in the hand of the drunkard, but slavery is in the hand of fools.
26:10All the flesh of fools is greatly storm-tossed, for their distraction is shattered.
26:11Like a dog that comes upon its own vomit and becomes hateful is a fool who has returned in his own wickedness to his own sin.
26:11aThere is shame that brings on sin, and there is shame that is glory and favor.
26:12I saw a man who thought himself wise, yet a fool had more hope than he.
26:13A lazy person sent on a journey says, “A lion is in the roads!”
26:14As a door turns on its hinge, so a lazy person on his bed.
26:15A lazy person, having hidden his hand in his lap, will not be able to bring it to his mouth.
26:16The lazy person appears wiser to himself than one who brings back a message in full.
26:17As one who grasps a dog’s tail, so is one who presides over another’s dispute.
26:18As healers put forward words to people, and the first to meet the word will be tripped up,
26:19so are all who ambush their own friends, and when detected say, “I did it in play.”
26:20With much wood a fire flourishes, but where there is no double-minded person, battle is quiet.
26:21A hearth for coals and wood for fire, and an abusive man for the turmoil of battle.
26:22The words of tricksters are soft, but they strike into the store-chambers of the inward parts.
26:23Silver given with deceit must be regarded like a potsherd; smooth lips cover a painful heart.
26:24A weeping enemy agrees to everything with his lips, but in his heart devises deceits;
26:25if the enemy entreats you with a loud voice, do not be persuaded, for seven evils are in his life.
26:26One who hides enmity establishes deceit, but one well known in councils discloses his own sins.
26:27One who digs a pit for his neighbor will fall into it, and one who rolls a stone rolls it upon himself.
26:28A false tongue hates truth, but an unrestrained mouth makes disorders.
